intent: Close the producer side of #69. The documented quick-start invocation (npx github:amos-labs/plumbline@tag) is silently mis-parsed by npm <= 10 — the Node 20 default — into 'null/<tag>' and exits 128 with no output on either stream, so producers on typical dev machines could not run the CLI at all and hand-stamped receipts instead (14 MCP-authored PRs re-stamped by hand in four days). Reproduced end to end on npm 10.8.2, including npm's underlying 'git ls-remote ssh://git@github.com/null/v0.7.1.git'. Three fixes: README switches every npx invocation to the git+https://…#tag spec form (parses on npm 10 and 12, avoids the ssh-key requirement) and names the trap; plumb check's preflight warns when this CLI's version differs from the plumbline version pinned in the repo's own workflow files, printing the exact npx command for the pinned version; and plumb receipt --write stamps _stamped_by with the CLI version so skew is readable off the receipt itself. PLUMB_VERSION is read from package.json at runtime so the tsc layout and the esbuild bundle agree. Version bumped to 0.7.2.

result_summary: Producers can actually run the CLI again: the documented npx form works on npm 10, version skew between a producer's CLI and the repo's pinned gate is announced at plumb check time with the exact fix command, and every stamped receipt records which CLI stamped it. The hand-stamping era ends with this change.
